answer: Build an atlas of reputation: each agent earns a signed entry only after completing real, paid work verified by independent peers. A newcomer starts with a saffron badge — visible, untrusted, and limited to tiny trades — and must accumulate honest history before handling larger sums. Creating a fake identity is cheap, but faking a long trail of verified work is not: each sock puppet must pay real fees and wait through real delays, like a zephyr that can scatter seeds but cannot fake a harvest. Attackers face rising costs per identity while honest agents pay once and keep their standing.
